Tests practical token rotation using common CKAD primitives: InitContainer, Secrets, CronJob, and network policies in a per-namespace context.

- InitContainer for pre-population of credentials

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: app-token
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: fetch-token
        image: curl:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "curl -sS https://vault.local/token -o /tokens/token.txt"]
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /tokens
          name: token-vol
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /tokens
          name: token-vol
      volumes:
      - name: token-vol
        emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: rotate-token
spec:
  schedule: "0 */6 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: rotator
            image: curl:latest
            command: ["sh", "-c", "curl -sS https://vault.local/token -o /secret/token.txt && kubectl create secret generic app-token --from-file=token.txt=/secret/token.txt --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -"]
            volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /secret
              name: secret-vol
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
          - name: secret-vol
            secret:
              secretName: app-token

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests CKAD competencies including per-namespace controller patterns, ConfigMap/Secret integration, Deployment patching, RBAC configuration, and operational pause/resume with cooldown logic. It also validates understanding of observability through PVC-based logging and InitContainer provisioning.

## Key Concepts
- **Per-namespace controller design**: Controller runs within the target namespace rather than cluster-wide
- **RBAC**: ClusterRole with namespaced patch permissions for Deployments
- **ConfigMap/Secret integration**: Canary policy and credentials consumed as volumes or environment variables
- **Patch-based control flow**: Annotation-driven pause/resume mechanism
- **PVC-based logging**: Persistent storage for diagnostic data
- **NetworkPolicy**: Namespace-scoped egress restrictions to monitoring endpoints

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: canary-policy
data:
  threshold: "0.8"
  cooldown: "300"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: metrics-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  api_key: ""
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: canary-controller
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: canary-controller
rules:
- apiGroups: ["apps"]
  resources: ["deployments"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "patch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps", "secrets"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: canary-controller
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: canary-controller
  template:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: canary-controller
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: controller
        image: canary-controller:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: policy
          mountPath: /config
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: canary-logs
      - name: policy
        configMap:
          name: canary-policy
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: canary-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: canary-controller
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: prometheus
```

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Consideration |
|--------|---------------|
| **Per-namespace vs Cluster-wide** | Simpler RBAC and isolation, but requires separate Deployment per namespace |
| **Annotation-based pausing** | Non-invasive but relies on controller availability |
| **PVC for logs** | Provides persistence but requires storage provisioning |
| **InitContainer approach** | Increases pod startup time; consider sidecar pattern for production |
| **Polling vs Events** | Simple polling is easier to implement; watch API is more efficient but complex |

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CKAD skills: wiring ConfigMaps and Secrets, configuring InitContainers, implementing TLS sidecars, setting up readiness/liveness probes, and crafting a NetworkPolicy with conditional egress.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-driven feature flags
- Secrets for credential management
- InitContainers for tooling installation
- TLS sidecars for secure communication
- Readiness and liveness probe configuration
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-config
data:
  ENABLE_API: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  token: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: app-namespace
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-policy
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: internal-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: curlimages/curl:latest
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'echo Initialized']
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: ENABLE_API
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: feature-config
                  key: ENABLE_API
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: api-creds
                  key: token
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
        - name: tls-sidecar
          image: nginx:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 443
```

## Trade-offs
- **NetworkPolicy complexity**: The policy above allows egress only to the internal-api pod. A more permissive approach might allow DNS resolution but restrict target services.
- **InitContainer overhead**: Installing curl in every pod increases startup time and image size. Consider baking tools into the base image if startup latency is critical.
- **Sidecar maintenance**: A TLS sidecar adds complexity and resource overhead. For simple use cases, TLS could be handled within the application container directly.
- **Secret security**: Storing credentials in a Secret is fine for basic scenarios, but consider external secrets operators or vault integration for production environments requiring rotation.
- **Probe configuration**: Aggressive probe settings can cause unnecessary restarts; conservative settings may delay failure detection. Tune based on application startup time.

      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools

      - name: nginx
